references.text: Both verses are part of Jotham's parable about trees seeking a king, where the trees approach different trees with the same request to rule over them.
The continuation of the parable where the fig tree responds to the request, just as the vine later responds in verses 12-13.
A parallel structure in the parable where the thornbush is finally asked to be king, after the fig tree and other trees have declined.
The song of the vineyard uses similar imagery of plants and trees as symbols for Israel and leadership.
Ezekiel uses tree parables to illustrate God's sovereignty over who rules, a theme similar to Jotham's parable.
Jesus curses the fig tree, demonstrating the fig tree's symbolic meaning in biblical literature as an image of fruitfulness and responsibility.
